content: The transcervical intrauterine route is frequently utilized for operative gynecological procedures in women. The vagina is a region of the body that naturally harbors a rich and diverse bacterial flora. Consequently, performing surgical procedures through the vaginal route may increase the risk of post-procedure infections. Prophylactic antibiotics could potentially help in reducing the likelihood of such infections following transcervical intrauterine procedures. The objective of this review was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of prophylactic antibiotics compared to placebo or no treatment in preventing infections in women undergoing transcervical intrauterine procedures. The search strategy employed was based on the Cochrane Menstrual Disorders and Subfertility Group (MDSG) search methodology. The databases searched included the Cochrane MDSG Specialised Register, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) in The Cochrane Library (up to August 2012), MEDLINE (1946 to August 2012), EMBASE (1980 to August 2012), PsycINFO (up to August 2012), CINAHL (up to August 2012), Biological Abstracts (1966 to August 2012), and AMED (1966 to August 2012). The inclusion criteria for this review were strictly limited to truly randomized controlled trials that compared the use of prophylactic antibiotics with placebo or no treatment for the prevention of infectious complications following transcervical intrauterine procedures. Trials that were not randomized or were pseudo-randomized were excluded from consideration. No data collection or analysis was performed because no eligible randomized controlled trials were identified during the search process. The main finding of this review is that no randomized controlled trials have been conducted to investigate the impact of prophylactic antibiotics compared to placebo or no treatment in women undergoing transcervical intrauterine procedures. In conclusion, there is currently no evidence from randomized controlled trials to determine the effectiveness of prophylactic antibiotics in preventing infections after transcervical intrauterine procedures. As a result, no definitive recommendations can be made regarding the use of prophylactic antibiotics for this purpose.
